label: Kiosk / ATM / self-service machine
summary: Public self-service machines: government service booths, bank ATMs, ticketing, check-in, self-checkout

options.question: Hardware touchpoints used in the flow?
Languages (include RTL languages such as Arabic if needed)?
Is there an accessibility or compliance standard to follow (for example ADA, EN 301 549, or a local government guideline)? Name it, or say none.

preview_screen: The welcome screen: a clear title, the two or three main service buttons at kiosk scale, a language switch and an accessibility button.
code_target: A fixed-size stage at the machine's screen size, with idle, timeout-warning and reset behaviour built in.
required_states: Inactivity timeout warning with a countdown and a Continue button
Session reset (return to start, data cleared)
Error with a clear next step and a staff-help option
Hardware prompts (insert card, take card, take cash, take receipt, scan document) for each chosen touchpoint
design_guidance: Design for strangers in a hurry, standing up, possibly with a queue behind them. One task per screen, plain words, no jargon.
Large targets, well beyond mobile sizes (a working default is about 20 mm physical size; confirm the screen's pixel density), with generous spacing to avoid mistaken touches.
No hover, no small gestures, no long press, no double tap.
Keep the primary controls in the lower-middle of the screen and within reach for a seated user; do not place critical controls at the top of a tall screen.
Every step shows how to go back or cancel. Destructive or irreversible actions confirm first.
Sensitive entry (PIN, ID number) is masked, with no personal data left visible after the session resets.
Show the hardware prompts visually and in text, pointing toward where the physical slot is.

checks: Every touch target meets the chosen size (about 20 mm physical or larger) and is spaced to avoid mistaken touches.
No flow depends on hover, long press, double tap or small gestures.
Every screen has a way back or to cancel, and irreversible actions confirm.
The idle, timeout-warning, session-reset, error, out-of-service and hardware-fault states are designed.
Each chosen hardware touchpoint has its own prompt screen telling the user what to do next.
Sensitive fields are masked, and the reset state shows no personal data.
Text and controls reach high contrast in a bright public setting, and the larger-text and high-contrast modes are designed when chosen.
If an RTL language is in scope, the layout, icons and progress indicators mirror correctly.
Controls needed by a seated user are within reach when the reachable layout is chosen.
If a compliance standard was named, each of its requirements that applies to the design has been checked and listed as met or not.
